item.description: By CCJLS Editors. The December 2024 Issue.

item.title: The Impact of State Laws on Officer-Involved Deaths (OIDs) | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Morgan J. Steele, Ziwei Qi. This study examined how U.S. Supreme Court jurisprudence and state-level restrictions shaped law enforcement’s use of force during arrests and defined reasonable force across various states.

item.title: A Judge Is the Person Who Decides Who Sings Better: Children’s Comprehension of Legal Terminology | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Ana Sacau-Fontenla, Joana Morais. This study examined whether children understand legal terminology commonly used at Portuguese courts.

item.title: 26(1) Front Matter | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By CCJLS Editors. The April 2025 Issue

item.title: Gendered Injustice: How Prosecutor Gender Impacts Perceptions of Defendant Culpability | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Morgan Stalcup, Jacqueline Lee & 2 more. This study investigates how prosecutor gender impacts perceptions of defendant culpability in the criminal court system.

item.title: Demystifying the Plea Process: Investigating Attorney Communications and Client Misconceptions | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Miko Wilford, Rachele Difava & 1 more. As the U.S. shifts to a plea-based system, defense attorneys act as negotiators. We surveyed 134 attorneys examining client meetings, common misconceptions, missing information, and how attorneys advise plea decisions.

item.title: 26(2) Front Matter | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By CCJLS Editors. The November 2025 Issue.

item.title: The New Actor: Artificial Intelligence in Criminology and Criminal Justice | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Mingxi Tong. This paper examines artificial intelligence as a unique “new actor” in criminology and criminal justice, challenging traditional frameworks that focus on perpetrators, victims, and the criminal justice system

item.title: From the Stonewall Inn to The Cuff: Legacies of the Past, Current Disparities, and LGBTQ Communities’ Complex Relationship with Police | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Valerie Jenness. This article focuses on the complex and fraught relationship between LGBTQ communities and law enforcement, historically and in the present.

item.title: Appellate Court Review of Sentencing Guideline Departures Through the Lens of Focal Concerns Theory | Published in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Law & Society
item.description: By Amanda R. Witwer. The present study examines departure review by the Michigan Court of Appeals in a sample of 124 opinions through the lens of focal concerns theory.
